clue.text: What a card! He's hidden by sightseer's murderer

indicators.note: something hidden by another thing is tucked inside it, so one word sits within the next

blocks.note: the jack is a playing card, the knave
a tripper is a day tourist; the 's links it to what follows

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a joker, followed by a tourist apparently concealing someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card' suggests a playing card in a game, and also a joker of a person; a tripper is British for a day tourist, and the pronoun slips in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack the Ripper is the notorious unidentified Victorian killer of Whitechapel, London.

clue.text: Put off by a dateline, unexpectedly

indicators.note: something arranged unexpectedly comes out in an order nobody planned, so the letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: A reader is surprisingly irritated by the date line printed on a document.
explanation.definitionFit: To be alienated is to be estranged or repelled, which is what being put off means.

clue.text: First known river crustacean

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the following word

blocks.note: a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: Reads as a naturalist's note on the earliest crustacean recorded in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'river' seems to be just the R abbreviation, but here it gives the whole word RILL, a brook.
explanation.definitionFit: Krill are tiny shrimp-like marine creatures, eaten in huge numbers by whales, and are true crustaceans.

clue.text: When nasty things are found in the dye

indicators.note: things found in a phrase are sitting inside its run of letters, crossing the word gap

blocks.note: the run inside these two words

explanation.surface: Asks when unpleasant impurities turn up in a batch of dye.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish-brown colouring made from a shrub's leaves, used on hair and skin.

clue.text: Householder once could have been rare type "A"

indicators.note: could have been suggests the letters might be reshaped into something else

explanation.surface: Speculates that some householder of the past belonged to an unusual blood group A.
explanation.walkthrough: Before the council tax, British households paid local 'rates', so a ratepayer was a householder; 'once' marks the term as dated.
explanation.definitionFit: Rates were a British property tax on homes, abolished around 1990, so householders were the people paying them.

clue.text: Green nut

blocks.note: first meaning: a pale yellowish-green colour
second meaning: an edible green-kernelled nut

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase, a nut that is green; in fact each word separately defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the nut from a small Asian tree and to the soft green shade named after its kernel.

clue.text: "SEX" splashed over morning papers

indicators.note: something splashed about is scattered, so its letters land in a new order
spread over another thing means wrapped around it, enclosing it

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline about sex plastered across the morning newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'papers' means newspapers in the surface, but here it means test papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Exam papers are the written tests sat by students, so exams can be called papers.

clue.text: Writing letter in similar style

blocks.note: first meaning: exchanging letters with someone

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures copying a letter in a matching hand; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the participle of keeping up a postal exchange and an adjective for things that match or are analogous.

clue.text: Then a great yell, cut short, erupted where people were having a row

definitions.text: where people were having a row

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the previous word is lopped off
something that erupted bursts out chaotically, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Describes an argument that broke out with a big shout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with 'cow' in the surface (a quarrel) but means rowing a boat; the Henley Royal Regatta is a famous rowing event on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: The regatta is a series of rowing races, so it is a place where crews row.

clue.text: There's nothing to restrict the view

blocks.note: zero, shaped like the letter O
to pinion is to bind someone's arms

explanation.surface: Complains that nothing stands in the way of the scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'view' looks like scenery, but it means a point of view.
explanation.definitionFit: A view in the sense of a belief or judgement is an opinion.

clue.text: Willing to try another tea

indicators.note: another version of a word is a different form of it, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: to test is to try out
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone eager to sample a different cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Willing' looks like eager, but it is read as 'having made a will'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dies testate has left a valid will, so they have done their willing.

clue.text: Learn about being close to an organ

indicators.note: about suggests turning things around and moving them, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Studying while sitting near a church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests a musical instrument, but it is a body organ, the kidney.
explanation.definitionFit: Renal means relating to the kidneys, so it describes things belonging to or near that organ.

clue.text: Dismay about salary increase being curtailed in assessment

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the first word wraps the next one
curtailed literally means having the tail cut off, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a raise is a pay rise

explanation.surface: Disappointment that a pay rise was cut back after a staff review.
explanation.definitionFit: An appraisal is a formal evaluation, such as an employee's performance review, which is an assessment.

clue.text: Instrument, one carried by leading performer

indicators.note: something carried by another is held within it, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: the star is the lead performer
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A musical instrument, one of which the headline act lugs around.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is a long-necked Indian string instrument, made famous in the West by Ravi Shankar.

clue.text: Rude actors got plastered

blocks.note: the cast is the company of actors

explanation.surface: Ill-mannered performers became drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastered' looks like slang for drunk, but it is the building sense of coating a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: To roughcast a wall is to coat it with a coarse plaster of lime and gravel; the past tense is unchanged.

clue.text: Oxymoronic pre-dinner drink?

blocks.note: setter's reading: an aperitif whose name pairs a word for 'not wet' with a liquid

explanation.walkthrough: An oxymoron joins contradictory words; a drink described as the opposite of wet fits, and a fortified Spanish wine is a classic aperitif.
explanation.definitionFit: Fino and similar dry sherries are traditionally served chilled as an aperitif before a meal.

clue.text: Dogs' date of birth remains confused without one

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken away
confused means muddled, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A vet's records for some dogs, with birth dates jumbled and one missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'Dogs'' carries the possessive apostrophe of the surface; read as a plural it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dobermans are a German breed of guard dog, named after the tax collector who bred them.

clue.text: Check theatre seat can be put into use again

blocks.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
the stalls are the ground-floor seats of a British theatre

explanation.surface: Inspect a theatre seat to see if it can be used again.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstall something is to set it up again so it can be used once more, like software or a fitting.

clue.text: One strange dose of ether

blocks.note: an anaesthetic dose numbs you, so it is a 'numb-er'

explanation.surface: A single peculiar shot of anaesthetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'NUMBER' must be read as 'numb-er', a thing that numbs; that is how a dose of ether fits.
explanation.definitionFit: One is the first integer not divisible by two, so it is an example of an odd number.

clue.text: Like you, I hear — love wine (French and English!)

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A wine-lover tells someone they are alike in loving French and English wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on sound: 'you, I hear' is 'ewe', so the answer means like a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovine means sheep-like, and a ewe is a female sheep, which 'you' sounds like when spoken.

clue.text: Unfortunately hated to get some return on unsafe structure

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled
return means going back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: An investor resents getting only a small yield on a shaky building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' looks like a financial yield in the surface; here it signals reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A deathtrap is a building or vehicle so dangerous that it could kill those inside.

clue.text: Courts extract some for repatriation

indicators.note: to extract some of a word is to pull out a portion of its letters

explanation.surface: Law courts take money from deportees to fund sending them home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courts' suggests law courts, but it means courtyards.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is an open central court of a Roman house or modern building; atria is its plural.

clue.text: Little boys put it up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: Small boys hold something up, as if in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the second word turns over; reversing the whole phrase gives nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Putti are the chubby naked infant figures, like cherubs, seen in Renaissance paintings and sculpture.

clue.text: Riblike structure found on the coast of Spain

blocks.note: first meaning: an anatomical or botanical rib
second meaning: the Spanish word for a coast

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a fossil found on a beach; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a costa is a rib or rib-like ridge, and in Spanish the same word names a coastline, as in the holiday resorts.

clue.text: Developing a crop from part of a coconut

indicators.note: developing means changing form as it grows, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A farmer grows a harvest from a piece of coconut.
explanation.definitionFit: Copra is the dried white kernel of the coconut, pressed to extract coconut oil.

clue.text: Poor Iranian, not one to embrace very blissful state

indicators.note: poor means in bad shape, so the letters are rearranged
not means without, so a letter is dropped
to embrace is to wrap arms around, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A destitute Iranian who will not welcome a state of bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism nirvana is the final release from suffering, and loosely any state of perfect happiness.

clue.text: Best quality pig food held in part of sailing ship

blocks.note: mast is fallen nuts such as beech nuts, fed to pigs

explanation.surface: Premium pig feed stored aboard a sailing vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held in' sounds like a container signal, but nothing goes inside anything; it only links the parts to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The topmast is the section of mast fixed above the lower mast on a square-rigged vessel.

clue.text: Amazingly, enthusiast's tact is transferred to friend

indicators.note: transferred means moved around, so these letters change places

blocks.note: a fan is an enthusiast; the 's is read as 'has'

explanation.surface: Surprisingly, a devotee's diplomacy is passed on to a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantastically means incredibly or astonishingly, the same as an adverb of amazement.
